wnba:TOR@PHX TOR +365 ML \u2014 REFUSED.does_not_accrue: no promotion, no estimator update, no change to the refusal rule
wnba:TOR@PHX TOR +365 ML \u2014 REFUSED.honest_accounting: the refusal was RIGHT on this instance. That is worth almost nothing as evidence: n=1, and a +365 price is supposed to lose roughly 78% of the time, so a single loss is the MODAL outcome for a bet that was correctly priced AND for one that was a mistake to skip. This settles nothing about whether the refusal rule is calibrated. What it does confirm is that the STATED reason — an unverified rotation state on two eliminated teams — was pointing at a real risk: Phoenix won by 32.
wnba:TOR@PHX TOR +365 ML \u2014 REFUSED.outcome: Toronto lost by 32. The refusal AVOIDED a full-unit loss.

WHAT_THIS_COHORT_ACTUALLY_SHOWS.magnitudes: BOTH home margins were under-projected, and by a lot: -12.79 and -28.57, bias -20.68 with MAE 20.68. The two residuals do not cancel because they point the same way. At n=2 that is not a bias finding, but it is the thing to watch: a model that picks sides correctly while systematically under-projecting their size will look good on moneylines and lose on spreads, which is exactly what happened to TOR +9.5.
